title: Substitute
text: Let $$x=2sin\left(\theta\right)$$. Then the integral becomes the integral of $$4cos^2\left(\theta\right)$$ with respect to θ.

title: Integrate and convert back
text: Use $$cos^2\left(\theta\right)=\frac{1+cos\left(2\theta\right)}{2}$$ to get $$2\theta+sin\left(2\theta\right)$$. Then use $$sin\left(2\theta\right)=2sin\left(\theta\right) cos\left(\theta\right)=\frac{x \sqrt{4-x^2}}{2}$$.
